current_answer: As of 19 October 2026, public evidence reviewed here does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. OpenAI Codex issue #55028 reports that one Windows Plus user could not find GPT-6.1 Sol in CLI 0.153.4 catalogs and received HTTP 400; after updating to CLI 0.163.0, the user reported that the model appeared and requests completed. The before and after tests used different effort settings (xhigh and high), one account is involved, and the serving model was not independently verified. This is an access/client/catalog report, not evidence that completed answers got worse or that an update fixed all users. OpenAI's help page says access to GPT-6.1 Sol depends on eligible paid plan, workspace settings, product surface, and rollout. BridgeBench's latest Opus 5.5 score remains within its own stated range; a separate Claude Code user report lacks fixed-task replication and coincides with a client-version change. Check status, plan/workspace, client version, and model catalog for failed requests. For a completed answer that seems weaker, compare the same task with model, surface, effort, tools, context, and correction work held or recorded.

catalogue_card.question: Did the GPT-6.1 Sol problem show model decline or an access failure?
catalogue_card.text: One Codex user reports a missing catalog entry and HTTP 400 on CLI 0.153.4, followed by access after an update to 0.163.0. Effort also changed, and the serving model was not verified. This is not proof of capability decline.

summary: No broad AI-model capability decline is established by this public-source review.
A Codex CLI catalog/request failure for one user stopped reproducing after a client update; the before and after effort settings differed.
OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol availability depends on eligible paid plan, workspace settings, product surface, and rollout.
BridgeBench reports Opus 5.5 at 105.8% of its first tracked score on 16 October, within its own 90–110% range for that private suite.
A separate Claude Code user report remains a narrow behavior lead with no fixed-task replication or verified serving path.
Check client version, catalog, plan/workspace, and status for request failures; evaluate completed answer quality with a same-task replay.
uncertainty: The Codex catalog/access recovery is one user report; the initial and later tests changed client version and effort, and the provider did not verify the served model.
The OpenAI status API snapshot showed all systems operational, but its metadata was last updated 16 October and aggregate status does not exclude account, client, or entitlement failures.
BridgeBench uses a private task set and composite score; its within-band result does not generalize to all Claude tasks or surfaces.
The Claude Code issue is account-level and lacks a fixed task, route attribution, or independent replication.
Fresh forum posts and competitor product claims are qualitative; they do not establish prevalence, detector accuracy, adoption, or revenue.
No matched multi-provider before-and-after capability evaluation is established by the sources reviewed here.
freshness_note: Reviewed 19 October 2026. This is a public-source watch, not a controlled multi-provider capability test.
